# REQ-DX-V1: world-class release DX and correctness for v1

Stakeholder: Callisto owner (sole maintainer); users releasing Rust, npm (incl. napi-rs) and Python monorepos.

Status: open. The command surface and release machinery exist, but verified correctness and integration gaps remain. [The findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md) records evidence and coverage; [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [sequencing plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json) track the work. Cargo real-registry tests now exist; they do not establish full production release-path coverage.

Why: Callisto's release engine is rigorous but its surface is confusing and its setup is heavy. Goal: a new repo goes from `callisto init` to its first published release in under 10 minutes, with one obvious release command and no known correctness bugs.

## Decided by the owner

- The main verb is `release`. Flow: `add` → `version` → `release`.
- `callisto release` publishes every package whose version has no release yet: registry publish, tag, forge release. `--dry-run` previews it on any branch.
- User-facing commands shown in `--help`: init, add, status, version, release, pre, snapshot, completions. Plumbing stays callable but hidden.
- `add` keeps both modes: interactive wizard on a TTY, flags for automation, clear error with the needed flags when neither.
- Breaking changes are fine pre-1.0; no external users.
- Current implementation scope is Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm (including napi-rs) and Python/PyPI. Keep architecture room for Go and C#/.NET/NuGet without implementing those adapters now.
- Prefer canonical ecosystem-qualified references and deliberate legacy migration over collision-triggered identity magic. Release ownership, native distribution identity, version authority and effects are separate responsibilities; the detailed proposal is [the scoped model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- Do not build a universal package manager, build scheduler, cross-language inference engine or persisted execution journal. Native tools/CI own compilation, packing and authentication.

## Done when

- `callisto --help` lists exactly the 8 user commands; each has one plain-language line.
- `callisto release --dry-run` with no flags prints the full plan on any branch; `callisto release` with no flags performs it locally with credentials in the environment.
- The CI split (plan → build → execute across jobs) works through `release` flags or hidden subcommands, and callisto's own workflow uses them.
- `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag`, `filter-plan` are removed; one plan implementation serves preview and execution and includes every check listed above.
- Text output uses colour/tables on a TTY, plain text when piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, no schema versions in text; `status` shows cascaded bumps.
- Verified defects in the findings register are fixed with regression coverage across affected siblings. CI runs the shipped runtime behavior; no shipped Cargo feature variants. Existing real local npm/Cargo/PyPI tests are retained, with skipped prerequisites distinguished from executed coverage and production binding/observation paths checked separately.
- `callisto init` detects ecosystems/packages, asks only intent (fixed vs independent; release artifacts if binaries exist), writes minimal config, and can write a GitHub workflow using `callisto-action` of <= 40 lines; a non-interactive mode exists.
- Supported fixtures cover separate native packages, dual Cargo/npm outputs, and the common co-located Cargo/Maturin version-authority case. Native dependency ranges/names, all affected lockfiles and built distribution metadata agree after versioning.
- A retry completes required missing effects without inventing a new version, even after tag creation or a partial Python/platform upload. Required outputs and shared public-announcement prerequisites are explicit; version/tag existence alone is not completion evidence.
- Generated workflows build/place only intended supported outputs and configure native authentication without registry secrets in plan/build jobs. This repo retains no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate; the reviewed merge remains the authorization.
- Fresh-repository runs measure init-to-first-publication against the existing under-ten-minute goal, including commit and credential steps. The supported/unsupported boundary is documented; no timing evidence is claimed until measured.

## Decisions still open

Authenticated private Python indexes and HTML-only indexes; npm dist-tag verification/promotion; universal registry checksum requirements; wrapper-specific bump severity; inferred-only/manual release commits under ADR 2; exact canonical-reference migration and release-owner wire representation. Record those choices before their implementation; do not make unstated preferences release gates.

Go major-qualified module paths/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are model examples, not promised runtime support or additional v1 gates.

## Out of scope

- Non-GitHub forges (later).
- Moon plugin (replaced by a proto plugin separately).
- Crate consolidation / license split.
- Production Go or NuGet adapters, arbitrary SCM-derived Python version backends, automatic foreign-registry dependency inference and cross-registry atomic rollback.
# V1 system findings

Baseline: main `07154021c` (0.10.2). This is an open findings register, not an implemented behavior spec: it lists unshipped defects and evidence gaps only. [Roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [execution guide](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Confirmed means reproduced against the main binary or established by the cited code path; the evidence column distinguishes them. No hosted publication, competitor execution or fresh-repo timing run has been performed.

## Open confirmed defects

| Finding | Evidence and consequence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-MATURIN | `Package::version_grammar`: two fresh co-located Cargo/Maturin repos, with matching static versions and Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions, both reproduce E007 from init/status. Separate-directory fixtures did not cover this layout. | T07 | WS-ID-09; proposed version authority |

## Integration risks and evidence gaps

- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes or the desired npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete when every built file is on the index; the generated build-matrix workflow seals the file set in a credential-free build job and compares digests, while Python-only workspaces stay unsealed. Universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).
- Fresh local Cargo/npm/PyPI repositories completed documented setup through release dry-run; npm packing and Cargo package inventory passed. Python artifact build was blocked on sandbox network access to `setuptools`, and no timings, credentials, registry publication or hosted release were exercised. The under-ten-minute first-published-release goal therefore remains unverified (T12-DX).
- Go v2/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are architecture examples only, not production support or new v1 gates (T07/T08/T12).

## Owner policy, not a defect verdict

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. Decide whether inferred-only/manual version releases belong in managed CI before changing that authority. Do not silently accept a reconstructed roster.

Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.

A failure to stage `pre.json` removal after stable finalization leaves the file in place, and a fresh `version` invocation refuses with E121 and manual recovery guidance. This fail-closed outcome is the selected policy, not an automatic-retry feature; an end-to-end regression verifies it.

  "Measure against the owner's existing under-ten-minute goal using local registry targets for repeatability and a separately authorized hosted self-release/publication for real service evidence. Do not claim local tests prove hosted credential/index behavior.",
  "Verify representative package installation, npm native addon load, Python wheel metadata/import and Cargo locked resolution. Maturin local/native support and unsupported generated CI must remain distinguishable.",
  "Use measured failures to improve only in-scope onboarding/docs; report blocker requiring owner choice instead of hiding setup time or publishing without approval. Run documentation/link checks and relevant CLI regressions after doc/example changes.",
  "Close the v1 evidence review only when applicable owner requirements are demonstrated, or report the exact unmet requirement. No arbitrary Go/NuGet gate, new hosted publication or support promise is authorized by this task."
 ],
 "commit_message": "docs(dx): record measured first-release onboarding",

  "T12"
 ]

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. Decide whether inferred-only/manual version releases belong in managed CI before changing that authority. Do not silently accept a reconstructed roster.

Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.

A failure to stage `pre.json` removal after stable finalization leaves the file in place, and a fresh `version` invocation refuses with E121 and manual recovery guidance. This fail-closed outcome is the selected policy, not an automatic-retry feature; an end-to-end regression verifies it.

content.content:
# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
test-moon:
    moon run :test
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Exercise the Release-PR action's real shell block with Git and GitHub API
# boundaries faked. This proves the script's control flow given a decision
# shape; it does not call the real `callisto` binary, so it cannot catch a
# mismatch between what Callisto actually serializes and what this script's
# jq expressions expect. See test-release-action-binary for that check.
test-release-action:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
test-release-action-binary:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

# Execute the release lifecycle at the real CLI boundary with fake registry,
# Git, forge, and attestation providers. This is deliberately separate from
# broad workspace tests so PR CI makes the release behavior evidence visible.
release-workflow-behavior:
    bash .github/tests/release-workflow-behavior/run.sh

# Re-captures the real provider responses under testing/fixtures/providers with
# read-only network GETs. Manual: review the diff and update PROVENANCE.md.
provider-fixtures:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh

# Manual and network-dependent, so deliberately not part of `ci`: re-fetches the
# live providers and asserts each fixture's SHAPE (status code, JSON key paths,
# ls-remote line kinds) still matches; content is never compared.
provider-contract:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh --check

# Run Clippy lints (warnings treated as errors) as a single workspace invocation.
# Moon's per-project `cargo clippy -p $project` tasks all lock the same shared
# target/ dir, so running them one-per-project serializes on Cargo's own build
# lock instead of parallelizing — a single --workspace invocation lets Cargo's
# internal job scheduler parallelize across crates instead.
lint:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Lint only projects affected by changes since the base branch. Uses moon's
# project graph to find affected crates, then lints them in one cargo
# invocation (not moon's per-project fan-out) to avoid Cargo's build-lock
# serialization while still skipping unaffected crates entirely.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Check code formatting compliance via moon
fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

# Format code automatically via moon
fmt:
    moon run :format

# Security advisory, ban, license & source check via cargo-deny (workspace root, one pass)
audit:
    cargo deny check

# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
machete:
    cargo machete

# Verify public Rust API SemVer breaking changes
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
fuzz target="parse_package_id":
    cargo fuzz run {{target}}

# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace

# Generate code coverage report via cargo-llvm-cov.
#
# Optional `threshold`: when set, fails if total line coverage drops below
# it (--fail-under-lines). The human-readable summary is always emitted
# before enforcing the threshold: LCOV output itself contains no aggregate
# percentage, and a failed CI gate must say what developers need to improve.
# Unset means informational only; `just ci` and CI both call `just coverage 90`,
# so a CI coverage failure always reproduces locally with the same invocation.
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    args=(--workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info)
    cargo llvm-cov "${args[@]}"
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{threshold}}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{threshold}}"
    fi

# Check per-crate line coverage against a threshold (default 90%). The
# workspace-total --fail-under-lines gate can pass while a small crate is
# far below threshold, since a few large crates dominate the total line
# count -- this catches that case. Requires profile data from a prior
# `cargo llvm-cov` run in this session (e.g. `just coverage` just ran, or
# CI's own coverage step ran first); does not re-run tests itself.
coverage-per-crate threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only > /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json
    report=$(jq -r '
        .data[0].files[]
        | select(.filename | test("/crates/"))
        | {crate: (.filename | capture("/crates/(?<c>[^/]+)/").c), count: .summary.lines.count, covered: .summary.lines.covered}
        | [.crate, .count, .covered]
        | @tsv
      ' /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json \
      | awk -F'\t' -v threshold="{{threshold}}" '
          {sum[$1]+=$2; cov[$1]+=$3}
          END {
            for (c in sum) {
              pct = (cov[c]/sum[c]*100)
              status = (pct+0 < threshold+0) ? "FAIL" : "pass"
              printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%.2f\t%s\n", c, sum[c], cov[c], pct, status
            }
          }
        ' | sort)
    echo "$report" | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%-25s lines=%-6s covered=%-6s cover=%6s%%  %s\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5}'
    echo "$report" | grep -q FAIL && exit 1 || exit 0

# Clean build targets, Moon task caches, and generated artifacts
clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean
    rm -f lcov.info callisto-schema.json

# Fast pre-commit hook validation (<500ms formatting check)
pre-commit: fmt-check

# Pre-push hook validation: formatting check plus clippy on affected projects only
pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected

# Install native Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks
hooks:
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-commit' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-push' > .git/hooks/pre-push
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push
    @echo "Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks installed successfully."

# Static security audit of workflows and actions (requires zizmor and ripgrep).
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Credential-free release workflow contract, policy, and policy mutant checks.
release-workflow-checks:
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh --self-test

# Workflow Contracts CI job minus actionlint and zizmor: pins, release
# contract/policy, artifact build script, the Release-PR action contract
# under a minimal PATH, and the installer verification-mode tests.
workflow-contracts: release-workflow-checks
    bash .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-release-artifact-build-script.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_contract.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_download_extraction_format.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_action_ref_version_resolution.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_crates_io_fallback.sh

# Every check CI runs except actionlint (Docker) and the binary-dependent
# release-PR decide contract and artifact preflight build. CI runs them as
# parallel jobs (callisto-ci.yml); locally they run in sequence.
ci: fmt-check lint test audit doc-check zizmor workflow-contracts release-workflow-behavior (coverage "90")
name: Callisto CI & Validation

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  workflow-contracts:
    name: Workflow Contracts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install workflow validation tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: ripgrep,zizmor@1.30.0
      - name: Lint workflow and action metadata
        # actionlint v1.7.12 predates GitHub's documented $/ self-repository
        # syntax. Keep all other actionlint diagnostics strict.
        uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint@sha256:9d36088643581e728c969f35141f88139fec77280b2be23c1f66f8e40e1025e7 # v1.7.12
        with:
          # Docker action arguments are passed directly, rather than through a
          # shell. Keep the exception as one argument so its regex is intact.
          args: -color -ignore=\$/.+
      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - name: Audit workflow and action security
        run: just zizmor
      - name: Verify workflow contracts
        run: just workflow-contracts

  fmt:
    name: Code Formatting (Moon & Just)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - run: just fmt-check

  clippy:
    name: Clippy Lints (Moon & Just)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: clippy
      - run: just lint
      - run: just doc-check

  test:
    name: Test Suite (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest
      # Real-registry e2e runs on Linux only; the tests skip elsewhere.
      - name: Install Verdaccio (real-registry npm e2e coverage)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: npm install -g verdaccio@6.10.4 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
      - name: Install pypiserver (real-registry PyPI e2e coverage)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        # legacy-cgi: pypiserver 2.4.0 imports `cgi`, removed in Python 3.13.
        # gunicorn: the test's `--server gunicorn` avoids a slow getfqdn() bind.
        # setuptools/wheel: the test builds with `--no-isolation` against this venv's build
        # backend, so no network fetch happens during `python -m build`; must be pre-installed.
        run: |
          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin/pip" install pypiserver==2.4.0 twine==6.2.0 build==1.4.4 legacy-cgi==2.6.3 gunicorn==26.2.0 setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Install cargo-http-registry (real-registry Cargo e2e coverage)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: cargo install --locked cargo-http-registry@0.1.8 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
      - run: just test
      - run: just release-workflow-behavior
      - name: Verify Release-PR action against the real callisto binary
        run: bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

  release-artifact-preflight:
    name: Release Artifact Preflight (${{ matrix.id }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: macos-arm64
            runner: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
            kind: cross
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - name: Build the production artifact recipe
        env:
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifact-preflight
        run: bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh

  coverage:
    name: Code Coverage & Test Report
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: just coverage 90
      # Non-blocking for now: the workspace-total gate above can pass while
      # a small crate is far below threshold (a few large crates dominate
      # the total line count). Visible in logs so regressions get noticed;
      # promote to a required check once existing per-crate gaps are closed.
      - run: just coverage-per-crate 90 || echo "::warning::one or more crates below 90% line coverage (non-blocking, see job log above)"

  security:
    name: Security & Advisory Audit (Moon & Just)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny
      - run: just audit

  validate:
    name: Validate Changesets & Workspace Status
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-validate

  release-asset-attestation:
    name: Release Asset Attestation
    # Fork PRs also receive a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and only lack secrets; same-repo-only is a cost/policy choice.
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ASSET: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
    steps:
      - name: Select the latest release
        id: latest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag=$(gh release list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --exclude-drafts --exclude-pre-releases --limit 30 \
            --json tagName,isLatest --jq '.[] | select(.isLatest) | .tagName')
          if [[ -z "$tag" ]]; then
            echo "::notice::no published release yet; skipping the release asset attestation check"
          fi
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Download the release asset
        if: steps.latest.outputs.tag != ''
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.latest.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release download "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$ASSET" --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          test -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/$ASSET"
      - name: Verify the attestation with the installer's flags
        if: steps.latest.outputs.tag != ''
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          verify() {
            gh attestation verify "$1" \
              --repo orin-dx/callisto \
              --signer-workflow orin-dx/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml \
              --deny-self-hosted-runners
          }
          verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/$ASSET"
          # Negative control: a modified copy must fail, so the pass above is not vacuous.
          cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/$ASSET" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tampered.tar.gz"
          printf 'x' >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/tampered.tar.gz"
          if verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/tampered.tar.gz"; then
            echo "::error::negative control failed: attestation verification accepted a tampered copy of $ASSET"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "negative control passed: the tampered copy was rejected"

toolUseResult.stdout:
# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
test-moon:
    moon run :test
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Exercise the Release-PR action's real shell block with Git and GitHub API
# boundaries faked. This proves the script's control flow given a decision
# shape; it does not call the real `callisto` binary, so it cannot catch a
# mismatch between what Callisto actually serializes and what this script's
# jq expressions expect. See test-release-action-binary for that check.
test-release-action:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
test-release-action-binary:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

# Execute the release lifecycle at the real CLI boundary with fake registry,
# Git, forge, and attestation providers. This is deliberately separate from
# broad workspace tests so PR CI makes the release behavior evidence visible.
release-workflow-behavior:
    bash .github/tests/release-workflow-behavior/run.sh

# Re-captures the real provider responses under testing/fixtures/providers with
# read-only network GETs. Manual: review the diff and update PROVENANCE.md.
provider-fixtures:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh

# Manual and network-dependent, so deliberately not part of `ci`: re-fetches the
# live providers and asserts each fixture's SHAPE (status code, JSON key paths,
# ls-remote line kinds) still matches; content is never compared.
provider-contract:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh --check

# Run Clippy lints (warnings treated as errors) as a single workspace invocation.
# Moon's per-project `cargo clippy -p $project` tasks all lock the same shared
# target/ dir, so running them one-per-project serializes on Cargo's own build
# lock instead of parallelizing — a single --workspace invocation lets Cargo's
# internal job scheduler parallelize across crates instead.
lint:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Lint only projects affected by changes since the base branch. Uses moon's
# project graph to find affected crates, then lints them in one cargo
# invocation (not moon's per-project fan-out) to avoid Cargo's build-lock
# serialization while still skipping unaffected crates entirely.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Check code formatting compliance via moon
fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

# Format code automatically via moon
fmt:
    moon run :format

# Security advisory, ban, license & source check via cargo-deny (workspace root, one pass)
audit:
    cargo deny check

# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
machete:
    cargo machete

# Verify public Rust API SemVer breaking changes
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
fuzz target="parse_package_id":
    cargo fuzz run {{target}}

# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace

# Generate code coverage report via cargo-llvm-cov.
#
# Optional `threshold`: when set, fails if total line coverage drops below
# it (--fail-under-lines). The human-readable summary is always emitted
# before enforcing the threshold: LCOV output itself contains no aggregate
# percentage, and a failed CI gate must say what developers need to improve.
# Unset means informational only; `just ci` and CI both call `just coverage 90`,
# so a CI coverage failure always reproduces locally with the same invocation.
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    args=(--workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info)
    cargo llvm-cov "${args[@]}"
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{threshold}}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{threshold}}"
    fi

# Check per-crate line coverage against a threshold (default 90%). The
# workspace-total --fail-under-lines gate can pass while a small crate is
# far below threshold, since a few large crates dominate the total line
# count -- this catches that case. Requires profile data from a prior
# `cargo llvm-cov` run in this session (e.g. `just coverage` just ran, or
# CI's own coverage step ran first); does not re-run tests itself.
coverage-per-crate threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only > /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json
    report=$(jq -r '
        .data[0].files[]
        | select(.filename | test("/crates/"))
        | {crate: (.filename | capture("/crates/(?<c>[^/]+)/").c), count: .summary.lines.count, covered: .summary.lines.covered}
        | [.crate, .count, .covered]
        | @tsv
      ' /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json \
      | awk -F'\t' -v threshold="{{threshold}}" '
          {sum[$1]+=$2; cov[$1]+=$3}
          END {
            for (c in sum) {
              pct = (cov[c]/sum[c]*100)
              status = (pct+0 < threshold+0) ? "FAIL" : "pass"
              printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%.2f\t%s\n", c, sum[c], cov[c], pct, status
            }
          }
        ' | sort)
    echo "$report" | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%-25s lines=%-6s covered=%-6s cover=%6s%%  %s\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5}'
    echo "$report" | grep -q FAIL && exit 1 || exit 0

# Clean build targets, Moon task caches, and generated artifacts
clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean
    rm -f lcov.info callisto-schema.json

# Fast pre-commit hook validation (<500ms formatting check)
pre-commit: fmt-check

# Pre-push hook validation: formatting check plus clippy on affected projects only
pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected

# Install native Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks
hooks:
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-commit' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-push' > .git/hooks/pre-push
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push
    @echo "Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks installed successfully."

# Static security audit of workflows and actions (requires zizmor and ripgrep).
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Credential-free release workflow contract, policy, and policy mutant checks.
release-workflow-checks:
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh --self-test

# Workflow Contracts CI job minus actionlint and zizmor: pins, release
# contract/policy, artifact build script, the Release-PR action contract
# under a minimal PATH, and the installer verification-mode tests.
workflow-contracts: release-workflow-checks
    bash .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-release-artifact-build-script.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_contract.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_download_extraction_format.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_action_ref_version_resolution.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_crates_io_fallback.sh

# Every check CI runs except actionlint (Docker) and the binary-dependent
# release-PR decide contract and artifact preflight build. CI runs them as
# parallel jobs (callisto-ci.yml); locally they run in sequence.
ci: fmt-check lint test audit doc-check zizmor workflow-contracts release-workflow-behavior (coverage "90")
name: Callisto CI & Validation

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  workflow-contracts:
    name: Workflow Contracts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install workflow validation tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: ripgrep,zizmor@1.30.0
      - name: Lint workflow and action metadata
        # actionlint v1.7.12 predates GitHub's documented $/ self-repository
        # syntax. Keep all other actionlint diagnostics strict.
        uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint@sha256:9d36088643581e728c969f35141f88139fec77280b2be23c1f66f8e40e1025e7 # v1.7.12
        with:
          # Docker action arguments are passed directly, rather than through a
          # shell. Keep the exception as one argument so its regex is intact.
          args: -color -ignore=\$/.+
      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - name: Audit workflow and action security
        run: just zizmor
      - name: Verify workflow contracts
        run: just workflow-contracts

  fmt:
    name: Code Formatting (Moon & Just)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - run: just fmt-check

  clippy:
    name: Clippy Lints (Moon & Just)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: clippy
      - run: just lint
      - run: just doc-check

  test:
    name: Test Suite (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest
      # Real-registry e2e runs on Linux only; the tests skip elsewhere.
      - name: Install Verdaccio (real-registry npm e2e coverage)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: npm install -g verdaccio@6.10.4 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
      - name: Install pypiserver (real-registry PyPI e2e coverage)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        # legacy-cgi: pypiserver 2.4.0 imports `cgi`, removed in Python 3.13.
        # gunicorn: the test's `--server gunicorn` avoids a slow getfqdn() bind.
        # setuptools/wheel: the test builds with `--no-isolation` against this venv's build
        # backend, so no network fetch happens during `python -m build`; must be pre-installed.
        run: |
          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin/pip" install pypiserver==2.4.0 twine==6.2.0 build==1.4.4 legacy-cgi==2.6.3 gunicorn==26.2.0 setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Install cargo-http-registry (real-registry Cargo e2e coverage)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: cargo install --locked cargo-http-registry@0.1.8 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
      - run: just test
      - run: just release-workflow-behavior
      - name: Verify Release-PR action against the real callisto binary
        run: bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

  release-artifact-preflight:
    name: Release Artifact Preflight (${{ matrix.id }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: macos-arm64
            runner: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
            kind: cross
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - name: Build the production artifact recipe
        env:
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifact-preflight
        run: bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh

  coverage:
    name: Code Coverage & Test Report
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: just coverage 90
      # Non-blocking for now: the workspace-total gate above can pass while
      # a small crate is far below threshold (a few large crates dominate
      # the total line count). Visible in logs so regressions get noticed;
      # promote to a required check once existing per-crate gaps are closed.
      - run: just coverage-per-crate 90 || echo "::warning::one or more crates below 90% line coverage (non-blocking, see job log above)"

  security:
    name: Security & Advisory Audit (Moon & Just)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny
      - run: just audit

  validate:
    name: Validate Changesets & Workspace Status
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-validate

  release-asset-attestation:
    name: Release Asset Attestation
    # Fork PRs also receive a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and only lack secrets; same-repo-only is a cost/policy choice.
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ASSET: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
    steps:
      - name: Select the latest release
        id: latest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag=$(gh release list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --exclude-drafts --exclude-pre-releases --limit 30 \
            --json tagName,isLatest --jq '.[] | select(.isLatest) | .tagName')
          if [[ -z "$tag" ]]; then
            echo "::notice::no published release yet; skipping the release asset attestation check"
          fi
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Download the release asset
        if: steps.latest.outputs.tag != ''
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.latest.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release download "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$ASSET" --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          test -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/$ASSET"
      - name: Verify the attestation with the installer's flags
        if: steps.latest.outputs.tag != ''
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          verify() {
            gh attestation verify "$1" \
              --repo orin-dx/callisto \
              --signer-workflow orin-dx/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml \
              --deny-self-hosted-runners
          }
          verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/$ASSET"
          # Negative control: a modified copy must fail, so the pass above is not vacuous.
          cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/$ASSET" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tampered.tar.gz"
          printf 'x' >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/tampered.tar.gz"
          if verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/tampered.tar.gz"; then
            echo "::error::negative control failed: attestation verification accepted a tampered copy of $ASSET"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "negative control passed: the tampered copy was rejected"

# Publishing: registry authentication

Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).

Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.

---

## npm

Two supported patterns.

### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`

Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with npm registry
  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  env:
    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
```

`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.

### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`

`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: '20'
    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.

### Choosing a pattern

| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
| Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |

### Provenance

Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.

---

## Cargo (crates.io)

Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:

```yaml
env:
  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
```

Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. In this repo, inject it only into `execute`.

---

## Python (PyPI)

Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):

```yaml
env:
  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
```

Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.

Map the generated workflow's `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_PASSWORD` in the publishing job. The secret name alone does not configure Twine.

### Generated Callisto workflows

Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.

Native publish hooks, including `prepare` and `prepublishOnly`, run unchanged with their usual publishing environment.

### Current Python support limits

Callisto supports static PEP 621 or Poetry versions with `python -m build` and Twine. Current limits:

- Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
- Without a sealed build, files an earlier attempt uploaded are matched by name, not by content: a rebuild is not always byte-identical. A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
- A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. ## npm

Two supported patterns.

### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`

Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with npm registry
  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  env:
    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
```

`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: '20'
    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local actions are commit-bound by the checkout. Every external GitHub action
# must use its full immutable commit hash; Docker actions must use an immutable
# content digest.
set -euo pipefail

status=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  reference=${line#*uses: }
  reference=${reference%% #*}
  reference=${reference//[[:space:]]/}
  # Workspace-relative and GitHub's self-repository references are bound to
  # local repository content; only external actions need an explicit pin.
  [[ "$reference" == ./* || "$reference" == '$/'* ]] && continue
  if [[ "$reference" == docker://* ]]; then
    valid='^docker://[^@[:space:]]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'
  else
    valid='^[^@[:space:]]+@[0-9a-f]{40}$'
  fi
  if [[ ! "$reference" =~ $valid ]]; then
    printf 'mutable or malformed external action reference: %s\n' "$line" >&2
    status=1
  fi
done < <(rg --no-heading --glob '*.yml' --glob '*.yaml' '^\s*uses:\s*' .github)
codeowners=.github/CODEOWNERS
if [[ ! -f "$codeowners" ]] \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/workflows/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners" \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/actions/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners"; then
  printf 'CODEOWNERS must cover .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/ with a real owner\n' >&2
  status=1
fi
exit "$status"

keyUsage=digitalSignature,keyEncipherment
extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth
EOF
openssl x509 -req -in srv.csr -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -out srv.pem -days 2 -extfile ext.cnf 2>/dev/null
openssl verify -CAfile ca.pem srv.pem

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
W=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad/r2/verify
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
cd "$W"
rm -rf pkgs && mkdir pkgs
export PKG_ROOT="$W/pkgs"
PORT=18443
(cd pypi_app && "$W/pyvenv/bin/gunicorn" -b 127.0.0.1:$PORT --certfile "$W/certs/srv.pem" --keyfile "$W/certs/srv.key" app:app > "$W/pypi.log" 2>&1) &
echo $! > pypi.pid
for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -s -o /dev/null --cacert certs/ca.pem https://localhost:$PORT/simple/ && break; sleep 0.5; done
echo "--- simple root (TLS, with CA)"; curl -sS --cacert certs/ca.pem -i https://localhost:$PORT/simple/ | head -5
echo "--- simple root WITHOUT CA (expect fail)"; curl -sS https://localhost:$PORT/simple/ 2>&1 | head -2
echo "--- PEP 691 Accept on unknown project"; curl -sS -i --cacert certs/ca.pem -H 'Accept: application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json' https://localhost:$PORT/simple/callisto-e2e-probe/ | head -8
# build a package and upload with real twine over TLS
rm -rf proj && mkdir -p proj/callisto_e2e_probe
printf '[build-system]\nrequires=["setuptools>=61"]\nbuild-backend="setuptools.build_meta"\n[project]\nname="callisto-e2e-probe"\nversion="0.1.0"\n' > proj/pyproject.toml
echo > proj/callisto_e2e_probe/__init__.py
(cd proj && "$W/pyvenv/bin/python" -m build --no-isolation --outdir ../dist >/dev/null 2>&1; ls ../dist)
export TWINE_USERNAME=x TWINE_PASSWORD=x
echo "--- twine upload WITHOUT CA (expect fail)"; "$W/pyvenv/bin/twine" upload --non-interactive --repository-url https://localhost:$PORT/ dist/* 2>&1 | tail -3
echo "--- twine upload with REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE"; REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE="$W/certs/ca.pem" "$W/pyvenv/bin/twine" upload --non-interactive --repository-url https://localhost:$PORT/ dist/* 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "--- simple index after upload, PEP 691 Accept"; curl -sS -i --cacert certs/ca.pem -H 'Accept: application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json' https://localhost:$PORT/simple/callisto-e2e-probe/ | head -20
echo "--- same, curl via CURL_CA_BUNDLE env (as callisto would spawn curl)"; CURL_CA_BUNDLE="$W/certs/ca.pem" curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://localhost:$PORT/simple/callisto-e2e-probe/
echo "--- same, SSL_CERT_FILE env"; SSL_CERT_FILE="$W/certs/ca.pem" curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://localhost:$PORT/simple/callisto-e2e-probe/
kill $(cat pypi.pid) 2>/dev/null; pkill -f "gunicorn -b 127.0.0.1:$PORT" 2>/dev/null; true

"""TLS-terminating TCP forwarder: tlsproxy.py LISTEN_PORT TARGET_PORT CERT KEY"""
import asyncio
import ssl
import sys

listen, target, cert, key = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]


async def pipe(r, w):
    try:
        while data := await r.read(65536):
            w.write(data)
            await w.drain()
    except Exception:
        pass
    finally:
        try:
            w.close()
        except Exception:
            pass


async def handle(r, w):
    try:
        tr, tw = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", target)
    except Exception:
        w.close()
        return
    await asyncio.gather(pipe(r, tw), pipe(tr, w))


async def main():
    ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
    ctx.load_cert_chain(cert, key)
    server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, "127.0.0.1", listen, ssl=ctx)
    async with server:
        await server.serve_forever()


asyncio.run(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Time init -> release --dry-run on a fresh scratch repo per ecosystem, with the real callisto binary.

usage: dx_timing.py ECOSYSTEM(cargo|npm|python) WORKDIR [PYTHON_FOR_BUILD]
Local-only: no registry, no credentials, no push.
"""
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CALLISTO = "/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/v1-research/target/debug/callisto"
eco, work = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2])
build_py = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None
shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
work.mkdir(parents=True)
env = {
    **os.environ,
    "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": "/dev/null",
    "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM": "/dev/null",
    "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "t", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "t@example.com",
    "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "t", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "t@example.com",
    "NO_COLOR": "1",
}
steps = []


def run(label, args, timed=True, check=True):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=work, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    if timed:
        steps.append((label, dt, p.returncode))
    if check and p.returncode != 0:
        print(f"FAILED {label}: rc={p.returncode}\n{p.stdout[-1500:]}\n{p.stderr[-1500:]}")
        report()
        sys.exit(1)
    return p


def report():
    total = 0.0
    print(f"== {eco} (debug binary) ==")
    for label, dt, rc in steps:
        print(f"{dt:8.3f}s  rc={rc}  {label}")
        total += dt
    print(f"{total:8.3f}s  TOTAL timed")


def w(rel, text):
    p = work / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p.write_text(text)


# ---- fixture: what a user already has before running init (untimed) ----
if eco == "cargo":
    w("Cargo.toml", '[workspace]\nmembers = ["crates/core", "crates/app"]\nresolver = "2"\n')
    w("crates/core/Cargo.toml", '[package]\nname = "dx-core"\nversion = "0.1.0"\nedition = "2021"\ndescription = "d"\nlicense = "MIT"\n')
    w("crates/core/src/lib.rs", "pub fn f() {}\n")
    w("crates/app/Cargo.toml", '[package]\nname = "dx-app"\nversion = "0.1.0"\nedition = "2021"\ndescription = "d"\nlicense = "MIT"\n\n[dependencies]\ndx-core = { path = "../core", version = "0.1.0" }\n')
    w("crates/app/src/lib.rs", "pub fn g() {}\n")
    w(".gitignore", "target\n")
    pkg = "dx-core"
elif eco == "npm":
    w("package.json", '{\n  "name": "dx-root",\n  "version": "0.0.0",\n  "private": true,\n  "workspaces": ["packages/*"]\n}\n')
    w("packages/core/package.json", '{\n  "name": "dx-core",\n  "version": "0.1.0"\n}\n')
    w("packages/app/package.json", '{\n  "name": "dx-app",\n  "version": "0.1.0",\n  "dependencies": {"dx-core": "^0.1.0"}\n}\n')
    w(".gitignore", "node_modules\n")
    pkg = "dx-core"
elif eco == "python":
    w("pyproject.toml", '[build-system]\nrequires = ["setuptools>=61"]\nbuild-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"\n\n[project]\nname = "dx-probe"\nversion = "0.1.0"\ndescription = "d"\nrequires-python = ">=3.9"\n')
    w("dx_probe/__init__.py", "\n")
    w(".gitignore", "dist\nbuild\n*.egg-info\n")
    pkg = "dx-probe"
else:
    sys.exit("bad ecosystem")

run("git init + first commit + origin (untimed prereq)", ["bash", "-c",
    "git init -q -b main && git remote add origin https://github.com/example/dx.git && git add -A && git commit -q -m initial"], timed=False)

# ---- timed: the documented flow ----
run("callisto init --yes --versioning independent --workflow", [CALLISTO, "init", "--yes", "--versioning", "independent", "--workflow"])
run("git add + commit (init output)", ["bash", "-c", "git add -A && git commit -q -m 'chore: callisto init'"])
run("callisto status", [CALLISTO, "status"])
run("callisto add --package X:minor --summary", [CALLISTO, "add", "--package", f"{pkg}:minor", "--summary", "Add feature"])
run("git add + commit (changeset)", ["bash", "-c", "git add -A && git commit -q -m 'feat: change'"])
run("callisto release --dry-run (pre-version: expect nothing/plan)", [CALLISTO, "release", "--dry-run"], check=False)
run("callisto version --emit-decision", [CALLISTO, "version", "--emit-decision", ".callisto/release-decision.json"])
run("git add + commit (release commit)", ["bash", "-c", "git add -A && git commit -q -m 'chore: release'"])
p = run("callisto release --dry-run (post-version)", [CALLISTO, "release", "--dry-run"])
steps_out = p.stdout
report()
print("--- release --dry-run output (post-version) ---")
print(steps_out[:1800])
wf = work / ".github/workflows/callisto-release.yml"
print("--- generated workflow lines:", len(wf.read_text().splitlines()) if wf.exists() else "none")
print("--- config:\n" + (work / "callisto.toml").read_text())
if eco == "python" and build_py:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    q = subprocess.run([build_py, "-m", "build", "--sdist", "--wheel", "--outdir", str(work / "dist")], cwd=work, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(f"{time.perf_counter()-t0:8.3f}s  python -m build (isolated, network) rc={q.returncode}")
    if q.returncode:
        print(q.stderr[-800:])

content.content:
| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
| `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |
| `[release.profiles]` | table | none | Legacy; only `profiles.production` is read, to migrate its `forge-repository` into the top-level key. Conflicting values between the two are a hard error. |

### `[[release.artifact]]`

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
```

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name. Two entries exist by default even with no `[registries]` table at all: `crates-io` (kind `cargo`) and `npm` (kind `npm`), both with no URL override.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | `"npm"` if omitted | Registry ecosystem |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |

An explicit registry entry still defaults `kind` to npm when omitted; requiring it is planned. For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
```

## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`

Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact `PackageId` (first matching rule wins, prefixed forms like `cargo/foo` take priority over bare `foo` regardless of declaration order). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is a glob `PackagePattern` and can match many packages at once; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact ecosystem-qualified id or bare name. `[[package-set]]`: glob pattern. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Production `callisto release` against a local TLS verdaccio, real npm. No credentials, no real registry.
set -uo pipefail
W=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad/r2/verify
CAL=/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/v1-research/target/debug/callisto
cd "$W"
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null NO_COLOR=1 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=t GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=t@example.com GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=t GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=t@example.com
export npm_config_update_notifier=false
rm -rf vdcfg && mkdir -p vdcfg/storage
cat > vdcfg/config.yaml <<'EOF'
storage: ./storage
self_path: ./storage
web:
  enable: false
url_prefix: https://localhost:14443/
log: { type: stdout, format: pretty, level: warn }
packages:
  '**':
    access: $all
    publish: $all
    unpublish: $all
EOF
(cd vdcfg && "$W/vd/node_modules/.bin/verdaccio" -c config.yaml -l 127.0.0.1:14873 > "$W/verdaccio.log" 2>&1) &
VD=$!
for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:14873/-/ping && break; sleep 0.5; done
python3 tlsproxy.py 14443 14873 certs/srv.pem certs/srv.key > tlsproxy_npm.log 2>&1 &
PROXY=$!
trap 'kill $VD $PROXY 2>/dev/null; pkill -f "node_modules/.bin/verdaccio" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
sleep 1
U=https://localhost:14443

R="$W/prod-npm"; rm -rf "$R" "$W/bare-npm.git"
cp -R "$W/dx-npm" "$R"
/usr/bin/git init -q --bare -b main "$W/bare-npm.git"
cd "$R"
cat >> callisto.toml <<EOF

[registries.npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "$U/"

[[package-set]]
match = "npm/*"
publish-to = ["npm"]
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "local registry binding"
mkdir -p "$W/gitwrap-npm"
cat > "$W/gitwrap-npm/git" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
args=()
for a in "$@"; do
  if [[ "$a" == "https://github.com/example/dx.git" ]]; then a="file://$BARE"; fi
  args+=("$a")
done
exec /opt/homebrew/bin/git "${args[@]}"
EOF
chmod +x "$W/gitwrap-npm/git"
export BARE="$W/bare-npm.git"
export PATH="$W/gitwrap-npm:$PATH"
printf '//localhost:14443/:_authToken=callisto-e2e\n' > "$W/npmrc-user"
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS="$W/certs/ca.pem" NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG="$W/npmrc-user"
echo "--- release --dry-run"; "$CAL" release --dry-run 2>&1 | head -12
echo "--- release"
( time "$CAL" release 2>&1 | tail -25 ) 2>&1
echo "--- registry metadata"
for p in dx-core dx-app; do curl -sS --cacert "$W/certs/ca.pem" $U/$p | python3 -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d["name"],list(d["versions"]))'; done
echo "--- remote tags"; /opt/homebrew/bin/git -C "$W/bare-npm.git" tag --list
echo "--- delete tags, rerun must adopt"; /opt/homebrew/bin/git tag -l | xargs -n1 /opt/homebrew/bin/git tag -d >/dev/null; /opt/homebrew/bin/git -C "$W/bare-npm.git" tag -l | xargs -n1 /opt/homebrew/bin/git -C "$W/bare-npm.git" tag -d >/dev/null
"$CAL" release 2>&1 | tail -8
grep -ci "PUT.*dx-" "$W/verdaccio.log"

7:workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml
69:ci_workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml
execute="$(sed -n '/^  execute:$/,$p' "$workflow")"
require_line "$execute" '    needs: [plan, build, release-candidate]' 'PR merge is the release approval; execute must depend directly on the plan and verified build, not a GitHub Environment gate'
require_line "$execute" '            cmp "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" "$build_dir/release-intent/release-intent.json"' 'execute must reject a build handoff whose immutable intent differs from planning'
require_line "$execute" '          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent' 'execute must download release-intent outside the workspace -- callisto release execute re-checks release trust before every dispatch, which fails closed on any untracked file in the worktree'
require_line "$execute" '          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-build' 'execute must download release-build outside the workspace -- callisto release execute re-checks release trust before every dispatch, which fails closed on any untracked file in the worktree'
require_line "$execute" '          path: release-source' 'execute must use an explicit release-source checkout'
require_line "$execute" '          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}' 'execution must pass the coordinator revision through an environment variable'
require_line "$execute" '          args=(--source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" --intent "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" --receipt "$receipt_dir/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA")' 'execute must pass the explicit source checkout, coordinator revision, and mandatory receipt path to the current Callisto coordinator'

ci_workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml
checkout_count=$(rg -n 'uses: actions/checkout@' "$ci_workflow" | wc -l)
credential_free_checkout_count=$(rg -n 'persist-credentials: false' "$ci_workflow" | wc -l)
if [[ "$checkout_count" != "$credential_free_checkout_count" ]]; then
  printf 'workflow contract failed: every Callisto CI checkout must disable persisted credentials\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

require_line "$version_pr" '          persist-credentials: false' 'version-pr never git-pushes -- it commits through the forge API -- so it must not persist Git credentials'

if ! rg -Fqx '      - run: just release-workflow-behavior' "$ci_workflow"; then
  printf 'workflow contract failed: PR CI must run the behavioral release workflow harness\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! rg -Fqx '  release-artifact-preflight:' "$ci_workflow"; then
  printf 'workflow contract failed: PR CI must preflight every production artifact build recipe\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! rg -Fqx '        run: just workflow-contracts' "$ci_workflow" \
  || ! rg -Fqx '    bash .github/tests/test-release-artifact-build-script.sh' justfile; then
  printf 'workflow contract failed: CI must test the shared release artifact build script\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! rg -Fqx '          - id: macos-arm64' "$ci_workflow" \
  || ! rg -Fqx '            target: aarch64-apple-darwin' "$ci_workflow" \
  || ! rg -Fqx '            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu' "$ci_workflow" \
  || ! rg -Fqx '            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl' "$ci_workflow"; then
  printf 'workflow contract failed: artifact preflight must cover all three product targets\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

execute="$(sed -n '/^  execute:$/,$p' "$workflow")"
require_line "$execute" '          persist-credentials: true' 'execute pushes the release tag with a plain git push (dispatch_tag) -- unlike every other job it has no other way to authenticate, so it must persist Git credentials'

if rg -n '^  environment-policy:$|^    environment: release$' "$workflow" > /dev/null; then
  printf 'release workflow contract failed: a merged release PR is the only approval; no Environment reviewer gate may delay execute\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

name: feedback-prove-with-the-real-tool
description: "Release, auth and registry paths need real-tool proof and adversarial testing before \"done\"; fake-tool tests and compile-only checks hid the 0.10.1 failure."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: f98f161c-abe7-472b-92f1-8cfe1cfdf74a
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:47:10.505Z
---

Do not call release-path, credential, forge or registry work done on the strength of fake-tool tests, a clean compile or green `just ci`. The 0.10.1 release failed with E140 because the runner stopped passing `GH_TOKEN` to `gh`; every test used a fake `gh` that never needed a token. The user then said they had "zero confidence" and asked for proof.

**Why:** the user lost a release attempt and trust. Earlier in the session the same pattern recurred: layered PRs that compiled but failed tests and docs checks, a Cargo fix whose tests only covered the matching case (an independent review found two real flaws), and a "pure move" refactor whose branches no test executed.

**How to apply:**
- For credentials, auth, forge and registry paths, reproduce the failure with the real tool (an empty config dir so no stored login can mask it) and run the fix through the real code path; make fake tools refuse to run without what the real one needs.
- Write the failing test first and confirm it fails on the old code (stash the fix, run, restore). Test adversarial inputs, not only the case being fixed.
- Before a refactor, check line coverage of the code being moved and add characterization tests for unexecuted branches.
- Read the real exit status of `just ci` (the log's `exit=` line); a background-task notice saying exit 0 is not the pipeline's result.
- State what is unproven. Say "probably fine and recoverable", not "100%".
- Run an independent adversarial review on risky changes before the user merges.
